answer: An agent economy mitigates Sybil attacks through microfluidic biochemical proof. A verifier challenges each node to optically analyze a droplet of floral nectar using an onboard crystal spectrometer. Treating identity as costless is a computational fable; an attacker must deploy discrete fluidic sensors and botanical feedstocks per agent instead of multiplexing virtual nodes. However, ambient temperature swings alter fluid viscosity, occasionally causing valid agents to fail verification.
